idea: Data room analysis support for small PE funds
buyer: Deal teams at sub-£500m PE funds
pain: Deal teams drown in data room material under time pressure
v1: One data room synthesis on a live deal
verdict: High fees and real pain, but PE deal teams are a segment she reaches by introduction and cycles are lumpy.

why.distribution: Reachable through her husband's IB network, but PE deal teams are not her own relationships.
why.demand: Funds already pay advisors heavily during diligence; the budget exists.
why.fmf: Rapid synthesis of unfamiliar businesses is her core skill, though private-deal diligence differs from public analysis.
why.revenue_structure: Deal by deal, entirely dependent on transaction flow.
why.defensibility: Accounting and strategy firms do this at scale with teams she cannot match.
why.leverage: Intense project labour on someone else's timetable - the least leveraged shape available.
why.time_to_revenue: Introductions plus waiting for a live deal: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: Deal volumes are cyclical rather than structurally growing.
why.ceiling: £15k x 14 deals = £210k, but deals arrive unpredictably and demand her full attention when they do.

ceiling_arithmetic: £15k x 14 deals = £210k. The constraint is that deals are lumpy and all-consuming: three concurrent diligences is impossible solo, so realistic year one is 4-6 deals = £60-90k.
carries: Genuinely high fees and an existing budget line.
kills: Leverage and lumpiness. She would be on call for other people's deal timetables with no ability to smooth the year.
test: Ask two PE contacts via her husband whether they would bring in a freelance analyst on the next deal.
test_fail: They use their existing advisors or juniors.
